$comment: The framework's document-head defaults, and when the document's own
declaration stands them down.
Two writers compose the head of a rendered page, and which one runs is
decided by where the page is served from rather than by anything the
project wrote:
- crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/static_assets.rs  (`dev`, `start`, and
every page a build pre-renders)
- packages/ruvyxa/runtime/entry-templates.mjs    (a request-time render
inside a deployed function bundle)
The second one only had the viewport half. A deployed build therefore
served its pre-rendered pages with an icon link and every request-time
render without one, so the browser fell back to `/favicon.ico` — which the
`ruvyxa.png` convention every scaffolded project ships does not answer.
One 404 per page load, on the deployments only, for the routes that are
hardest to notice are missing it.
Every implementation replays this file:
- crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/static_assets.rs        (Rust test)
- tests/packages/ruvyxa/document-head-parity.test.mjs  (JavaScript test)
`assetLinks` is what the build resolved from the project's public files;
the deployed writer is handed the same string through the deploy manifest
rather than deriving it again, so only the stand-down rule below is
written twice and this is what holds the two copies equal.
$standDownNote: Both quote styles, for all four spellings. A document that declares any
icon keeps its own set whole rather than being merged with the framework's
— a project shipping `ruvyxa.png` beside its own mark used to get both
links, and the framework's was the one the browser answered.
The quote styles were not equal before this file existed: the native
writer matched `rel='icon'` but not `rel='shortcut icon'`, so a document
using single quotes for the longer spelling was given a second icon.

cases.name: a document that declares neither gets both
cases.expect: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="/ruvyxa.png">

cases.name: a project that publishes no icon gets only the viewport
the document's own viewport stands the default down
a single-quoted viewport is the same declaration
an upper-case attribute is the same declaration
rel=icon stands the icon link down
single-quoted rel=shortcut icon stands it down
an upper-case rel is the same declaration
a document declaring both keeps both of its own
a rel this rule does not cover is not an icon declaration
cases.expect: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><link rel="icon" type="image/png" href="/ruvyxa.png">
